chapter.title: Introduction to Cloud Computing
chapter.summary: An overview of cloud computing concepts, service models, and deployment strategies used in modern enterprise environments.

section.heading: What is Cloud Computing?
section.paragraph: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services including servers, storage, databases, networking, software, and analytics over the internet.
It enables faster innovation, flexible resources, and economies of scale. Organizations typically pay only for the cloud services they use.

section.heading: Service Models
section.paragraph: There are three primary service models in cloud computing that every architect must understand before designing solutions.

subsection.heading: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
subsection.paragraph: IaaS provides virtualized computing resources over the internet. It is the most flexible cloud computing model, giving users full control over their infrastructure.
subsection.example: Amazon EC2, Microsoft Azure VMs, Google Compute Engine

subsection.heading: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
subsection.paragraph: PaaS delivers hardware and software tools over the internet, typically for application development. The provider hosts the hardware and software.
subsection.example: Google App Engine, Heroku, Microsoft Azure App Service

subsection.heading: Software as a Service (SaaS)
subsection.paragraph: SaaS delivers software applications over the internet, on demand, and typically on a subscription basis.

section.heading: Deployment Models
section.paragraph: Organizations choose from four primary deployment models based on their security, compliance, and operational needs.
section.note: The choice of deployment model significantly impacts cost, security posture, and operational complexity.

chapter.title: Security in the Cloud
chapter.summary: Comprehensive guide to securing cloud environments, covering identity management, encryption, and compliance frameworks.

section.heading: Shared Responsibility Model
section.paragraph: Security in the cloud is a shared responsibility between the cloud provider and the customer. Understanding this boundary is critical.
section.warning: Misunderstanding the shared responsibility model is one of the leading causes of cloud security breaches.

section.heading: Identity and Access Management
section.paragraph: IAM is the foundation of cloud security. Proper configuration of IAM policies prevents unauthorized access and privilege escalation.

subsection.heading: Principle of Least Privilege
subsection.paragraph: Every user, service, and application should have only the minimum permissions required to perform its function. Excess permissions are a liability.
